key_insight: A 3D COMSOL multiphysics model shows that the n-ZnSe/p-SrScCu3Se4/p+-WSe2 heterostructure can reach high photovoltaic efficiency, with optimized opto-electro-thermal behavior driven by absorber and defect engineering.
engineering_relevance: This study provides a realistic device-design roadmap for high-performance quaternary chalcogenide solar cells by linking geometry, doping, defects, and heat generation to output metrics.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and thermal loss
Parametric sweeps of absorber width, acceptor level, and bulk defects
evidence_signal: Under optimized conditions, the device achieved VOC = 1.02 V, JSC = 32.472 mA/cm2, FF = 88.212%, and PCE = 29.217%, with QE strong in the visible but weaker in the near-infrared.
watch_item: The reported performance is simulation-based, so experimental validation and tolerance to fabrication defects, interfaces, and thermal nonuniformity remain important concerns.
paper_title: Computational analysis and performance optimization of SrScCu3Se4-based solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics
